alternatives.argument: Goodman--Wallach Cor. 7.1.6 (p. 333) proves that the outer multiplicity of V^λ in a finite-dimensional module F equals ∑_{s∈W} sgn(s) dim F(λ+ρ−s·ρ) by comparing the coefficients of e^{μ+ρ} on the two sides of A(ρ)ch F = ∑_μ mult_F(V^μ) A(μ+ρ) (their Prop. 7.1.4 and Cor. 7.1.6 proof, pp. 332--334). This is precisely the coefficient extraction at the dominant translate used by the lemma; no Humphreys text is needed.

Goodman--Wallach Cor. 7.1.7 (pp. 333--334) substitutes the weight-multiplicity decomposition (5.59) into Cor. 7.1.6 and proves mult_{V^μ⊗V^ν}(V^λ) = ∑_{t∈W} sgn(t) m_μ(λ+ρ−t(ν+ρ)), which after renaming λ↔ν is exactly the stated Steinberg formula with the weight multiplicities m_μ of the second factor. Knapp Problem 17 (pp. 611--612, solution pp. 747--748) derives the same expression in the sgn/μ∨ form from the Weyl character formula.

With F = V^λ⊗V^μ in Cor. 7.1.6, its expansion termwise groups the Steinberg sum by φ = ν+ρ−w(λ+ρ); a regular φ has a unique dominant conjugate with sign and an irregular φ contributes 0 (the vanishing ∑_{σ∈W} sgn(σ)ε_{σ(φ)} = 0 for weights fixed by a reflection, Knapp Problem 16 and GW's coefficient comparison). Knapp Problems 17--21 (pp. 611--612, solutions pp. 747--748) state and use exactly this regrouping: χ_λχ_{λ'} = ∑_{λ'' weight of τ_λ} m_λ(λ'') sgn(λ''+λ'+δ) χ_{(λ''+λ'+δ)∨−δ}, with sgn = 0 on walls.
